newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: First Quantum starts Zambia mine development.
newsitem.headline: First Quantum starts Zambia mine development.

text.p: Canada's First Quantum Minerals Ltd has begun development work at Zambia's Bwana Mkubwa mine in the country's Copperbelt Province -- the first private mine in Zambia in 25 years, the company said on Monday.
First Quantum representatives in Lusaka said construction work had started to revive the copper mine at Ndola, abandoned by owners Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) in 1984.
"The construction of the project will take 15 months," Bwana Mkubwa director Kwalela Lamaswala told Reuters. "It is expected that Bwana Mkubwa will start production by April 1998."
The project involved construction of a plant to recover copper from tailings -- estimated to be in the region of 8.4 million tonnes -- deposited by previous operations.
Initial production was estimated at 10,000 tonnes of copper a year for a five-year period. This would generate income of around $100 million.
Bwana Mkubwa Ltd is a private company registered in May 1996 and owned by First Quantum.
"This will be the first private sector mining company to come on stream in Zambia in over 25 years," Lamaswala said.
The project would have an estimated capital cost of $26 million for plant construction, and a further $3 million of working capital allowance.
The project could earn Zambia $21.8 million in copper exports per annum.
Zambia is currently in the throes of a privatisation drive, which would see the mining and power assets of ZCCM -- the largest public enterprise in the country -- sold.
